scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can retrieve a paginated and filterable list of discussion board sections with advanced search and sorting. The API should correctly return a list of sections filtered by a specific configuration ID, name, enabled status, and order, as well as properly handle pagination (limit, offset), and complex sorting requests. Prepare at least two sections in the system—with different names, configurations, and enabled states—before testing. Edge cases: querying with non-existent filter values (should return empty), invalid pagination boundaries (large offset), and sorting by non-standard columns (should return validation error if not supported).

dependencies.purpose: Create initial sections with varying configurations, names, and enabled values for list filter coverage.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a single discussion board section by valid and invalid sectionId. First, create a section and fetch its record by its ID, verifying the returned data matches what was created (including configuration reference, name, order, and enabled fields). Then, attempt to retrieve a section using a random UUID not linked to any section, confirming that a 404 'not found' error is returned. This validates both normal operation and error handling for invalid or unauthorized access.

dependencies.purpose: Create a discussion board section and capture its ID to use in a successful GET scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of a new discussion board section with valid properties, including a valid discussionboard_configuration_id, unique name, description, order, and enabled flag. Ensure the section is created successfully and the returned record has all expected values. Then, attempt creation with a duplicate name (unique per table) for the same or another configuration—expect a uniqueness constraint violation error. Also, attempt creation with an invalid discussionboard_configuration_id to confirm that a foreign key constraint error is raised. Edge cases: missing mandatory fields (should trigger validation errors).

dependencies.purpose: Create a configuration to reference by discussionboard_configuration_id when creating valid and invalid sections.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing section's properties (configuration reference, name, description, order, enabled) with valid data—ensure changes persist and are reflected in the updated record. Also, attempt to update with a name that duplicates another section's name (should fail with uniqueness error), and attempt to update the configuration reference to a non-existent configuration (should return a foreign key error). Finally, test updating a section that does not exist to confirm proper error handling (404 not found).

dependencies.purpose: Create possible configuration(s) in preparation for update and re-assignment scenarios.
Create at least two sections—one for a successful update, one to test duplicate name and reference changes.

scenarios.draft: Test the permanent deletion (hard delete) of an existing discussion board section. First, create a section, delete it, and verify the operation succeeds and the section is no longer retrievable. Then, attempt to delete a section with a non-existent sectionId and confirm that a suitable error (e.g., 404 not found) is returned. Optionally, test cascade effects (if any exist in categories or related records).

dependencies.purpose: Create a section to use for a successful delete operation.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated list of discussion board categories as an admin without specifying any filters or sort options. Expect a default paginated result with all active (enabled) categories, validating pagination and basic accessibility. Verifies that the endpoint returns records and proper pagination fields even when no filters are set.

Test filtering the discussion board category list by name and enabled status. Create several categories with varying names and enabled values. Then, request a paginated list filtered to a specific name and enabled=true, and verify only matching category records are returned. Confirm filter logic works and irrelevant records are excluded.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple categories with different names and enabled flags for search filter validation.

scenarios.draft: Test paginated retrieval of categories with explicit limit, offset, and sorting by the order field. Bulk-create more categories than will fit on a single page, set different order values, and request a particular page sorted by 'order' descending. Verify correct ordering and page slicing logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create a bulk set of categories with various order values for sorting/pagination scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a single discussion board category by its unique id as an admin. Create a category, capture its id, then retrieve it via GET. Verify that all fields match what was created and that the category is present. Verifies happy path access to detail endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Create the discussion board category to retrieve, and get its id.

scenarios.draft: Test handling of a request for a non-existing discussion board category id. Attempt to retrieve a category using a random/non-existent UUID and verify that the API returns a 404 not found error.

Test successful creation of a discussion board category with valid data, including all required fields (discussionboard_section_id, name, order, enabled). Confirm that the new category is properly stored and returned with all expected fields, and that the returned object matches the input data. Ensures happy path creation for admin workflows.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new section to be associated via discussionboard_section_id with the new category.

scenarios.draft: Test category creation failure due to missing required fields such as name or discussionboard_section_id. Attempt to create a category omitting each required property in turn and confirm the API returns validation errors and does not create the record. Verifies required field enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create a section for valid discussionboard_section_id when other fields are purposely omitted.

scenarios.draft: Test category creation with an invalid or non-existent discussionboard_section_id. Attempt to create a category with a section ID that does not exist and verify the API returns a foreign key constraint failure or validation error. Checks enforcement of referential integrity.

Test successful update of a discussion board category by id. Create a category, then update properties such as name, description, order, and enabled status using the PUT endpoint. Verify updated fields are persisted and the response reflects the changes. Validates basic update mechanism for admin category management.

dependencies.purpose: Create the initial category to update and acquire its id.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a discussion board category using a non-existent categoryId. Provide valid update data but a random/nonexistent UUID. Verify the API returns a not found (404) error and no record is changed. Ensures robust error handling for wrong id updates.

Test update with an invalid discussionboard_section_id (not existing in sections table). Attempt to change the category's parent section to a non-existent section and expect a validation or foreign key error. Validates referential integrity enforcement on update.

dependencies.purpose: Create the initial category to update.

scenarios.draft: Test hard deletion of a discussion board category by id. Create a category, then delete it permanently via DELETE. After deletion, attempt to access the deleted category and confirm that a 404 not found error is returned. Ensures that records are removed and not recoverable via GET after deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create a category record to delete and capture its id.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion of a category using a non-existent id. Attempt to delete a category with a random or non-existent UUID and confirm the API returns a 404 error and does not affect existing records. Validates not-found error handling on DELETE for idempotency and safety.

Test retrieving a paginated, filtered list of admin role assignments as an authorized admin. The test should include scenarios where results are filtered by admin assignment creation date, id, and should confirm correct pagination. Verify that only schema-defined fields are returned and that unauthorized users cannot access this endpoint. Verify edge cases such as requesting a page beyond result set and filtering with no matches.

Test retrieving a list of admin assignments when no admin assignments exist in the system. The system should return an empty paginated result, and the response should meet all contract expectations. Confirm behavior for newly deployed or purged environments.

Test successfully retrieving the details of an admin role assignment by valid id as an authorized admin user. First, create an admin assignment and then fetch it using its id. The returned data should contain only the schema-defined fields (id, created_at), and all values should match what was created.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin assignment to obtain a valid id for retrieval testing.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to fetch an admin assignment by a non-existent or deleted id. The system should return a 404 error. Edge cases include fetching after deletion and using random UUIDs.

Test creating a new admin role assignment using a valid user/member id by an authorized admin actor. Verify that the new admin assignment record is returned with all schema fields populated. Confirm that creation with duplicate id or invalid user id is handled with the right business logic and error messages, such as conflict or foreign key constraint violation.

Test failure to create an admin assignment when providing a user/member id that does not exist in the referenced user/member system. The response should indicate failure due to foreign key or data integrity constraint, preventing role escalation for non-existent users.

Test updating an authenticated admin user's own assignment record with allowed changes (id and created_at fields only). Verify that updates are correctly processed and only authorized fields are changeable. Mutations to non-schema or immutable fields must be rejected. Requires the target assignment to exist & belong to the current user.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin assignment as the authenticated user to set up an editable record.

scenarios.draft: Test rejecting update attempts for admin assignments that do not belong to the authenticated user or that do not exist. The API should return permission denied (if not owner) or not found errors as appropriate.

Test deleting an admin user's own assignment with a valid id. The assignment should be permanently removed (hard delete), and future retrieval by this id should return not found. Verify audit trail logic is unaffected, and subsequent actions as admin are restricted after assignment is deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin assignment for the current user to set up the scenario for self-deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling for attempts to delete an admin assignment not matching the authenticated user or one that does not exist. System must reject with permission denied or not found errors, protecting assignment integrity and system security.

Test the retrieval of moderator warning logs using diverse filters, search criteria, and pagination. Prepare several warning log records with varying moderator_ids, warned_member_ids, reasons, and issued_at timestamps. Execute multiple queries: filtering by specific moderator, warned member, reason keyword, date ranges, and combination filters. Test pagination controls (limit, offset/page) and sort results by issued_at both ascending and descending. Verify correct filtering, sorting, search hit, and pagination adherence as per input. Edge case: filter by non-existent reason or member should return empty result set. Validate that all results match schema and only include actual warning logs, no extra data.

dependencies.purpose: Create several warning log records with different fields to allow filter and repeatable querying of search/list endpoint for business logic and data presence.

scenarios.draft: Validate that a moderator can retrieve full warning log details by its unique id. Create a warning log entry as a prerequisite. Attempt to fetch it by id and confirm all schema fields (id, moderator_id, warned_member_id, warning_reason, issued_at) are present and accurate. Also verify that requesting a non-existent id returns a proper 404/not found error. Attempt to fetch a log belonging to another moderator (ownership not enforced for this endpoint) to confirm admin/mod visibility. Document business rule for policy compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new warning log to obtain a valid id for successful retrieval test. Simulate other moderator-created logs to check cross-access scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that an admin can retrieve any moderator-issued warning log record by its PK id. Create logs as different moderators and then use the admin endpoint to fetch by id, checking that the full warning log data is present (id, moderator_id, warned_member_id, warning_reason, issued_at) and matches the original. Attempt to retrieve a non-existent or deleted id to confirm error handling. Validate that admin access semantics are enforced regardless of log creator or recipient.

dependencies.purpose: Create warning logs with different moderator_id and warned_member_id values to provide a test set for admin retrieval and error handling scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a warning log by a moderator. Provide valid moderator_id, warned_member_id, warning_reason, and issued_at. Upon creation, fetch the log to verify all data is saved correctly. Confirm that all required schema fields are present in the returned record and that unique PK is generated. Business rule: creation is restricted to authorized moderators and proper relations must exist for the referenced member. Also, attempt creation with a missing required field to verify validation error messages are returned.

Ensure that an admin can create a warning log entry for any targeted member by providing moderator_id, warned_member_id, reason, and issued_at. Create as admin, then retrieve to verify storage. Test creation with duplicate or conflicting data (same moderator warns same member for same reason at same time) and confirm system's uniqueness or business constraints. Validate failure when providing non-existent member ids or invalid moderator ids (if validation is enforced at business logic layer). Edge: creation with extremely long or blank warning_reason should be validated appropriately.

Test retrieving a paginated list of content reports using a variety of filter and pagination options (e.g., status, report_reason, reported_at range, reporter_member_id, moderator_note, and search terms if supported). Verify that filtered search returns only matching records with correct pagination, that sort direction is honored, and that edge cases such as no results, large page sizes, or invalid filter criteria are handled gracefully with appropriate error or empty result responses.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one content report as a member to ensure there is data to query. This step must be executed before retrieval to guarantee known data exists in the system.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can retrieve the full details of a specific content report by id. This includes validating returned fields (report_reason, status, moderator_note, reporter data, etc.) match what was created. Also test that the endpoint rejects requests when the id does not exist (404 error) or if the report id is malformed. Confirm that only correct schema fields are present in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a content report as a member to obtain a valid report id for detail lookup.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve the full details of a specific content report by id, ensuring that all schema fields are present and correct. Validate that errors are properly returned when the id does not exist and that the response is strictly limited to allowed fields. Also test edge case: attempt to access a report belonging to another actor to ensure appropriate permissions/enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create a content report to supply a real report id for the admin detail retrieval test.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a content report by a logged-in member, providing all required schema fields (reported_post_id, reporter_member_id, report_reason, status, reported_at). Confirm that the created record matches the supplied data, the ID is generated, and the status is as expected. This should also validate business logic such as required fields and correct references. Also, attempt to create a report for a non-existent post to trigger a foreign key constraint violation and verify the error is meaningful.

Test creation failure when a member submits a content report request omitting required fields (e.g., missing report_reason or reported_post_id). Validate that the API rejects the request with validation errors that correctly specify which fields are missing or invalid.

Test that attempting to create a content report as a member using a reported_post_id that does not exist triggers a foreign key constraint error or a similar error indicating the post is invalid. Confirm correct error code and message are returned.

Test successful creation of a content report by a guest user with all specified schema fields (reported_post_id, reporter_guest_id, report_reason, status, reported_at) present. Confirm that the returned record matches the payload and that the guest is properly identified as the reporter. Also, validate business rules (such as guests not being able to impersonate members).

Test that a guest attempting to create a content report with an invalid or non-existent reported_post_id receives a meaningful error response, validating foreign key enforcement and error messaging. This ensures that guests cannot report non-existent content.

Test listing suspensions with different combinations of filters, pagination, and search criteria. Ensure that filtering by moderator_id, suspended_member_id, suspension_reason, suspension_started_at, and suspension_ends_at works as expected. Check that paginated results represent total record counts accurately and that sorting returns records in the expected order. Also, test error cases such as providing invalid filter values or using unsupported fields in the request body. Only admin or moderator roles should be able to access this endpoint; attempting with unauthorized roles must yield a forbidden error.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least two suspension records with distinct moderator_id, suspended_member_id, and suspension_reason fields for filter variety. Requires moderator permissions to initiate suspensions before testing listing as admin.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a single suspension record by its id (UUID) via moderator endpoint. Confirm correct details are returned for a valid id, including moderator_id, suspended_member_id, suspension_reason, suspension_started_at, and suspension_ends_at, matching those set at creation. Test error scenarios: attempt to retrieve a non-existent suspension id to verify not found error, and attempt with insufficient permissions to confirm authorization handling.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid suspension record as a moderator to use its id in the retrieval test.

scenarios.draft: Validate that an admin can fetch details of a single suspension entry by its UUID. Confirm returned data corresponds to the fields created: correct moderator_id, suspended_member_id, reason, start and end timestamps. Test not found scenario by passing a random or previously deleted/non-existent id, expecting an appropriate error response. Confirm forbidden error on access attempts by unauthorized roles or lacking admin/moderator privileges.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one valid suspension record as an admin to use its id for successful retrieval testing.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a new suspension by a moderator with all required and valid fields: moderator_id, suspended_member_id, suspension_reason, suspension_started_at, and suspension_ends_at. Verify the returned record matches the provided data and is persisted in the system for subsequent listings. Test error conditions such as attempting to create a suspension using an invalid member_id (non-existent user), missing required fields, invalid or past suspension date ranges, and unauthorized role attempts.

Verify that an admin can create a new suspension by providing valid moderator_id, suspended_member_id, suspension_reason, suspension_started_at, and suspension_ends_at according to schema rules. Ensure successful creation returns all fields correctly, and that the record appears in list retrievals. Negative test: try to create a suspension without required fields or with invalid UUIDs, and confirm validation errors. Attempt creation with non-admin role to confirm access restriction handling.

Test fetching a paginated and filtered list of member entities. Register multiple discussionboard_members via the creation endpoint, varying their created_at timestamps. Then, request a paginated list using various filters (id, created_at range) and check that only matching members are returned, in correct paginated order. Confirm total counts and validate that access is restricted to authenticated members only.

dependencies.purpose: Register multiple member entities needed for realistic search, filter, and pagination logic.

scenarios.draft: Test requesting a member list with a filter that does not match any records (e.g., filtering by a non-existent id or impossible created_at range). Confirm that the result is an empty list, and no errors are thrown.

dependencies.purpose: Register one or more members to ensure system is initialized; then search with impossible filter to force empty result.

scenarios.draft: Test successfully retrieving a member's information by valid id. First, register a member and obtain the unique id, then fetch this member via the GET endpoint and confirm returned data (id, created_at) matches the original registration. Ensure access control for members only.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member and get the id needed for target GET request.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a member by an invalid or non-existent id. Register a new member, then attempt to fetch a member using a random/incorrect uuid (not present in the system). Confirm the system responds with an appropriate not found error or access error if unauthorized.

dependencies.purpose: Register a valid member to establish initial state and compare error behavior using an invalid id.

scenarios.draft: Test successful member registration with valid id (uuid) and proper timestamp. Ensure that after registration, the member can be listed and retrieved by id using the appropriate endpoints. Validate the created_at timestamp is correctly set and associated with the provided id.
Test member creation failure by attempting to register two members with the same UUID. The system should reject the second creation with a duplicate key error, enforcing uniqueness on the id field.

dependencies.purpose: Register the first member to set up the duplicate id scenario; the second registration should reuse the same id and expect failure.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a member's created_at field for maintenance or correction purposes. Register a new member, then update the created_at value using the PUT endpoint. Confirm the returned member contains the updated timestamp and correct id. Ensure only self-owned members can be updated, and errors are thrown for unauthorized access.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account to obtain the initial data and id for update.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a member using an id that does not belong to the authenticated user. Register member A and member B (separate ids), then, while authenticated as member A, attempt to update member B's id. Confirm the system denies access and returns the correct error message for forbidden or not found.

dependencies.purpose: Register two members to set up ownership boundary checks.

scenarios.draft: Test successfully deleting a member's own record by id. Register a member, then delete it using this endpoint. After deletion, attempts to fetch the member by GET should return not found or access error. Validate that no personally identifying or profile data is returned after deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member and retrieve their id to set up the delete test.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion failure when trying to delete another member's record. Register two members, A and B. While authenticated as member A, attempt to delete member B's id. Confirm the system rejects the action due to ownership or access constraints.

dependencies.purpose: Register both member A and member B to check ownership enforcement in deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of a paginated, filtered, and sorted list of moderator assignments by an admin. The scenario should verify that filtering moderators by schema fields (id, created_at) returns only valid moderator assignments and supports pagination/sorting. Confirm proper access control and that only admin role can perform the operation.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a moderator assignment via admin before listing to ensure at least one record exists for testing filtering and search.

scenarios.draft: Test failure retrieving the moderator assignment list when the admin authentication is absent or invalid. The test should confirm that access is denied for unauthorized roles or unauthenticated users and responds with a relevant error indicating lack of permission.

Test successful retrieval of a single moderator assignment by valid id as an admin. The process should first create a moderator assignment, then retrieve it using its id, verifying that all schema fields (id, created_at) are correctly returned and accessible to admin roles.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid moderator assignment as a test data setup, so a known id is available for single assignment retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when attempting to retrieve a moderator assignment by an id that does not exist. This should verify the system returns a not found (404) error when the specified id does not correspond to any moderator assignment in the database.

Test successful creation of a moderator assignment with a valid id (which may reference a real user/member in other domains/tables). Ensure that an admin can create the moderator role assignment, and verify that all schema fields are properly set in the response.

Test failure when attempting to create a moderator assignment with an id that does not correspond to any existing user. The system should return an error indicating that the referenced user/member does not exist, ensuring foreign key constraints are enforced or relevant validation errors are provided.

Test successful update of the authenticated moderator's assignment using only schema-allowed fields (id and created_at). The scenario should verify the update can be performed only by the owner via the /my/ path, and only permitted fields are changed, returning the fully updated assignment record.

dependencies.purpose: Setup: Admin creates a moderator role assignment so the member has an assignment to edit via the /my/ endpoint.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when the moderator attempts to update their assignment with fields not present in the schema. The API should return a validation error for extra or non-permitted fields, ensuring schema compliance is strictly enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Prerequisite: The moderator assignment must exist so that the update operation can be invoked.

scenarios.draft: Test error scenario where a moderator attempts to update a moderator assignment that does not belong to them (i.e., where their authentication does not match the assignment owner). The system must return an appropriate forbidden or unauthorized error, enforcing ownership rules.

dependencies.purpose: Setup: Create a moderator assignment that does NOT belong to the authenticated moderator for negative access testing.

scenarios.draft: Test successful hard delete of the authenticated moderator's own assignment by id. The scenario should verify that the record is permanently removed when called by the owner via the /my/ route and that subsequent retrieval attempts return not found (404).

dependencies.purpose: Setup: Admin creates the moderator assignment. Moderator then deletes their own assignment using its id.

scenarios.draft: Test error case when a moderator attempts deletion of a moderator assignment that they do not own. The API should return a forbidden or unauthorized error, ensuring only the authenticated moderator can delete their assignment.

dependencies.purpose: Setup: Create a moderator assignment not owned by the current moderator, used to test access restrictions on delete.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an authenticated member can retrieve a paginated and filtered list of guest records. Prepare a set of guest records by creating several guests with varying created_at timestamps. Test basic listing, searching by guest id, filtering by date ranges, and using pagination (limit/offset) parameters. Validate that the system returns only id and created_at fields per schema. Also verify system properly rejects requests using unauthorized roles and omits unauthorized data. Boundary cases include empty result sets and results at page-size limits.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple guest records to ensure there is test data for pagination and filtering.

scenarios.draft: Validate that listing guest records returns an empty list when there are no guest records present in the system. Ensure the system properly handles the case and responds with correct pagination metadata.

Test retrieving a guest record by a valid, existing id. First, create a guest record and then fetch it using its id. Confirm that both the id and created_at fields are returned and match the original creation values.

dependencies.purpose: Create a guest record to obtain a valid id for retrieval test.

scenarios.draft: Validate that trying to fetch a guest record by a nonexistent id returns the appropriate error. Use a freshly generated UUID that does not exist in the database. Confirm system behavior for not-found cases aligns with platform error response policy.

Test successful creation of a guest record. Provide all required fields (id, created_at) with valid values and verify that the system returns the created record including id and created_at values. Ensure no additional fields are accepted and system ignores any extraneous data.

Test that attempting to create a guest record with an id that already exists results in a uniqueness violation error. First, create a guest with a specific id, then attempt to create another guest with the identical id and confirm the system returns the correct error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a guest with a specific id to set up a duplicate creation attempt.

scenarios.draft: Validate the system rejects creation requests that omit one or both required fields (id, created_at). Attempt to create guest records with missing id, missing created_at, and with both fields missing. Confirm the API returns field validation errors in each case.

Test that an authenticated member can update the created_at field of their own guest record. First, create a guest record. Then, update the created_at timestamp for that record. Verify only allowed fields are accepted and id is immutable. Confirm that the updated created_at is returned in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a guest record to update during the test.

scenarios.draft: Verify the API rejects any attempt to update the id field of a guest record, which is the primary key and must remain immutable. Create a guest, then attempt to change its id with a PUT request. Confirm a validation error is returned and the database value does not change.

dependencies.purpose: Create a guest record to test immutability of id field during update.

scenarios.draft: Validate that a user cannot update a guest record they do not own. Create a guest record associated with a specific member identity, then attempt an update as a different member and confirm the API returns a forbidden or not-authorized error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a guest record under one member identity for another member to attempt updating.

scenarios.draft: Test successful hard-deletion of a guest record by its owner. Create a guest record then perform a DELETE request using its id as the authenticated member. Verify the record is permanently removed from the database and is no longer retrievable.

dependencies.purpose: Create a guest record to be deleted during the test.

scenarios.draft: Validate deleting a guest record with a non-existent id returns an appropriate error and does not affect any data. Attempt DELETE with a randomly generated UUID not associated with any guest record.

Confirm that users cannot delete guest records they do not own. Create a guest with one member session, then attempt to delete it as a different member. Confirm the API responds with a forbidden or not-authorized error and the record remains.

dependencies.purpose: Create a guest under one member to attempt deletion as another member for permission validation.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated list of posts with various filters and pagination options. Start by guaranteeing the existence of multiple threads and posts (including parent and reply posts) with different bodies, is_edited, is_deleted flags, and a range of created_at values. Make several requests using filters such as filtering by thread ID, filtering for only posts that are not deleted, or searching for text in the body. Verify that results are paginated correctly, that sorting works as expected, and that the filter logic returns only posts matching the specified criteria.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more threads to associate posts with.
Create several posts (including replies) using different combinations of thread, parent_post_id, and flags to enable comprehensive filter and search testing.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a post's full details by ID. First, create a post and retrieve it by its ID, verifying that all returned fields match the creation and that no extraneous data is present. Then attempt a request with a non-existent or malformed ID to ensure the API returns a 404 or validation error as appropriate. Also check that posts marked as is_deleted can still be retrieved (not hard deleted).

dependencies.purpose: Ensure a thread exists for associating with the test post.
Create a post (and optionally a reply) to test single post retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test successful post creation with valid data, including root posts and replies. Attempt to create posts with missing required fields (e.g., missing discussionboard_thread_id or body) to test validation error handling. Create reply posts by specifying parent_post_id and verify hierarchical relationships in the database. Attempt to create a post referencing a non-existent thread or parent_post_id and confirm that appropriate foreign key errors are returned. Also create posts as replies to a post marked is_deleted and confirm reply creation is supported for deleted posts (soft-delete case).

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread for root post creation.
Create the parent post when testing reply creation.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member can update their own post's mutable fields ('body', 'is_edited', 'updated_at'). First, create a user, a thread, and a post. Then perform an update as the owner and verify changes are stored. Attempt to update immutable fields or provide fields not in the schema to confirm validation rejections. Also attempt to update a post as a different member and ensure the API rejects the unauthorized update attempt. Try to update a post that does not exist and verify proper error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread for post association.
Create a post belonging to the member for authorized updates.
Optionally create a second member profile to test unauthorized update attempts.

scenarios.draft: Test soft deletion (by setting is_deleted=true) of a member's own post. First, create a post, then call the delete endpoint and verify is_deleted is set and the post remains in database but is excluded from normal listing if required by spec. Attempt to soft delete a post owned by another member and verify access is forbidden. Attempt to soft delete a non-existent post ID and verify that a suitable error is returned. Also check that deleting a post already marked is_deleted is idempotent or errors appropriately.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread for post association.
Create a post for soft delete operations.
Optionally create a second member profile to test deletion of posts not owned by the current user.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated list of discussion threads, filtering by category. First, create at least two threads—each in a different discussionboard_category. Then, use this endpoint to query for threads in one specific category with pagination and verify only the relevant thread is returned and pagination metadata is correct. Ensure unrelated threads are excluded from the result set.

dependencies.purpose: Create several threads in different categories to ensure that filtering and pagination provide meaningful and differentiable results. This must be done first to provide actual data for list and filtering tests.
After test thread creation, call this endpoint for category-filtered and paginated retrieval; used to verify business logic for visibility and correct filtering of threads.

scenarios.draft: Test listing threads by searching on title keyword. Create a thread with a unique keyword in the title. Then query using the search option for that keyword and verify the thread appears in the response, no unrelated threads are present, and pagination still works as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a thread whose title includes a distinctive keyword, allowing the search feature to be accurately tested.

scenarios.draft: Test searching for threads using a filter value that matches no records. Issue a query on the list endpoint for a non-existent combination of category, status, or title. Confirm that the paginated results contain an empty data set and the metadata reflects zero total items.

Test successful retrieval of an individual thread by ID. First, create a thread. Then query this endpoint with the thread's id. Validate that all thread fields match the created data, including title, status, category ID, and other metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread whose id will then be used to verify successful detail retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to retrieve a thread with a non-existent id. Call the endpoint with a random or deleted thread id and confirm a not found (404) response is returned.

Test creation of a new discussion thread with valid data. Supply all mandatory fields with correct values, including category ID, title, status, created_at, and confirm a successful response returns the complete thread object as per schema.

Test creation failure when omitting required fields (such as title or category id). Submit a POST request with incomplete payload and verify the response returns the appropriate validation errors, listing the missing required fields.

Test thread creation with an invalid or non-existent category id. Attempt to create a thread referencing a random or deleted category id. Verify that the operation fails and the error code or message reflects foreign key constraint or invalid reference.

Test successful update of a member's own thread. First, create a thread as the authenticated user, then call this endpoint to update mutable schema fields such as title and status, and verify changes are saved in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread owned by the authenticated member that will then be updated. This ensures ownership is properly tested.

scenarios.draft: Test update attempt using a non-existent or unauthorized thread id. Call the endpoint with a random or foreign id and expect a not found or forbidden response indicating the user can't update the thread.

Test failure when attempting to update fields not allowed by schema (such as immutable fields like id or created_at). Include these immutable fields in the update payload and confirm that the system rejects the request with corresponding validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread so an update can be attempted with forbidden fields, testing business rules enforcement for mutable vs immutable properties.

scenarios.draft: Test the soft deletion (archiving) of a member's own thread. Create a thread, then delete it via this endpoint. Afterwards, retrieve the thread and confirm its archived field is set to true and the thread is not included in default list queries.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread to test the soft delete/archiving process.

scenarios.draft: Test attempt to delete (archive) a thread not owned by the authenticated user. Attempt to delete a thread created by another user. System should respond with forbidden or not found error, confirming business logic for ownership enforcement.

Test deleting (archiving) a thread that is already archived. Archive a thread, then attempt to archive it again. Confirm that the endpoint either idempotently returns success or gives a specific error indicating the thread is already archived and cannot be re-archived.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread, archive it, then attempt to archive again—testing duplicate archival edge case.

scenarios.draft: Test a member retrieving their active authentication sessions with valid pagination and filters. The request should retrieve only the sessions linked to the authenticated member, using legitimate filter and sorting criteria on fields like issued_at and status. Validate that pagination and filter options are properly enforced, and that only sessions the member is authorized to view are returned.

Ensure that requesting authentication session list with an invalid filter field (e.g., referencing a non-schema property) results in a validation error. The server must reject any filters or sorts not defined in the discussionboard_auth_sessions schema.

Verify that the authentication session list returned only includes sessions owned by the authenticated member. Pre-create a session for another member and verify this session is never shown to the requesting member, ensuring proper isolation between users' session data.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session for a different member. Required to ensure cross-user isolation.

scenarios.draft: Retrieve a single authentication session by its ID and validate that all returned fields match the schema definition. Pre-create a session and attempt to fetch it by its generated ID, confirming all actual session fields (id, actor_type, actor_id, issued_at, expires_at, last_activity_at, revoked_at, ip_address, user_agent) are present in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session to produce a valid id for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to fetch an authentication session by a non-existent ID and verify that the API returns a not-found error.

Try to retrieve a session which exists but does not belong to the requesting context (e.g., another user's session if permissions are enforced at the session level). Ensure that proper access control is enforced or that the session is simply not found.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session belonging to another user (different actor_id) to verify access restrictions.

scenarios.draft: Create a new authentication session with all required fields (actor_type, actor_id, issued_at, expires_at, ip_address, user_agent). Validate that the returned record matches the schema and has properly stored all fields.
Attempt to create a session with one or more required fields omitted. Validate that the API returns appropriate validation errors for each missing field.

Verify that the API does not allow creation of two sessions with the same ID, as IDs must be unique in the schema. Create a session, then attempt to create another session reusing the same id and expect a conflict or validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial session to produce a duplicate id condition.

scenarios.draft: As an authenticated member, update own session record with valid updatable fields (last_activity_at, revoked_at, expires_at, ip_address, user_agent). Ensure only schema fields are mutable and the changes are reflected in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session record for updating during the test.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update an authentication session with a field not present in the schema (e.g., deleted_at). Confirm that the API rejects the update as invalid.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session record to use for invalid update attempts.

scenarios.draft: Try to update a session record that does not belong to the authenticated member. Expect a forbidden or not-found error, confirming proper ownership enforcement in session updates.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session record for a different member to test ownership enforcement.

scenarios.draft: As an authenticated member, delete own authentication session by id. Validate that the session is permanently removed from the database (no soft-delete) and can no longer be retrieved.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session for the authenticated user in preparation for testing deletion.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete an authentication session which does not belong to the authenticated member. Confirm that the API enforces ownership and responds with an error or not-found, ensuring only own sessions can be deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session for a different member to test access restriction on delete.

scenarios.draft: Delete an authentication session, then attempt to delete the same session again to validate that the API properly returns a not-found error for redundant delete attempts.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session, then delete it before re-attempting deletion for error handling check.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a list of poll votes as an admin with advanced filtering, pagination, and sorting options. Ensure results are filtered as expected by poll ID, voting member ID, selected option, and created_at. Validate that only fields present in the schema are filterable. Include tests for both typical filter values (e.g., poll exists with votes, members who have voted) and edge cases (such as filtering results for a non-existent poll or a poll with no votes). Also, confirm paging behavior and ordering of records. Failure scenarios should include unauthorized access attempts by non-admin users and invalid filter criteria (e.g., incorrect field names or types).

dependencies.purpose: Create a poll to ensure there is a valid poll with which votes can be associated.
Create at least one poll vote record for an existing poll, by a member, so that the list endpoint can return non-empty data for valid filters.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving the details of a single poll vote by id as the voting member. Validate that when the poll vote exists and belongs to the requesting member, all schema fields are returned correctly. Confirm appropriate error handling when the vote does not exist or when the requesting member is not the owner (forbidden or not found errors). Include scenarios where the id is malformed or not a UUID. Validate that only authenticated members can access this endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Create a poll to associate vote entries with a valid poll.
Cast a poll vote as a member and obtain its id for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving the details of a poll vote by id as a moderator. Ensure all schema fields are accessible, and confirm the vote can be accessed even if not cast by the moderator. Include scenarios for when the poll vote exists and when it does not (expect not found error). Test error conditions such as using an invalid id or attempting access with insufficient permissions. Confirm that the endpoint reflects auditor access for moderation/review, as well as handling pagination if part of a review process.

dependencies.purpose: Create a poll to enable creation of poll votes for review.
Create one or more poll votes to be retrieved by the moderator for audit.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving the details of a poll vote by its id as an admin. Validate correct retrieval of all schema fields when the poll vote exists, and appropriate error responses for non-existent poll vote ids. Include negative cases for invalid id format and ensure correct permission requirements are enforced. This scenario also includes verifying that admin users can access any poll vote for auditing or compliance purposes.

dependencies.purpose: Create a poll for the purposes of associating votes to be audited.
Cast a vote on an active poll to generate a poll vote record for detail retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of a poll vote by an authenticated member on an eligible poll. Success scenario: member votes on an open poll and receives confirmation with all expected schema fields. Failure scenarios: attempting to vote on a closed/expired poll (expect error), voting twice on the same poll (expect unique constraint or duplicate error), submitting an invalid selected_option (violating business constraints), or providing an invalid poll id (not found or foreign key error). Confirmation must be made that the vote is only recorded if all schema and business logic conditions are satisfied. Verify proper authentication enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create an active poll which will accept votes.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a post history snapshot as an admin by providing a valid post history ID. Ensure the response includes all fields defined by the schema and the correct snapshot data is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to allow for subsequent editing and history creation.
Edit the post as a member to generate a post history snapshot.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to retrieve a post history snapshot with a non-existent ID. Ensure the API returns a suitable error (such as a 404 Not Found) and the error information is clear in the response.

Test updating the authenticated member's own post history snapshot by ID. Provide valid update data for an allowed field such as edit_reason or edit_type, and verify that the changes are correctly reflected in the returned object. Ownership must be enforced so only the editing member may update their snapshot.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as a member for editing.
Edit the post to generate a post history snapshot that belongs to the member.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to update a post history snapshot not owned by the authenticated user. The API must reject the request with a forbidden or unauthenticated error, validating strict ownership enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as Member A.
Have Member A edit the post to create a post history snapshot.
Create a post as Member B to have a different member context for the attempted update.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a post history snapshot while attempting to change immutable or non-existent fields (such as id or created_at). The API must reject such updates and return a validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as a member for editing.
Edit the post to generate a post history snapshot.

scenarios.draft: Test hard deleting the authenticated member's own post history snapshot by ID. After successful deletion, verify that the snapshot is no longer retrievable and the operation is irreversible.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to permit creating a post history snapshot.
Edit the post to create a post history snapshot.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to delete a post history snapshot that does not belong to the authenticated member. The API must return a forbidden or unauthorized error, ensuring only owner may delete their snapshot.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as Member A and generate a post history snapshot.
Create a post as Member B for a different member context (attempt unauthorized delete).

scenarios.draft: Test deleting a post history snapshot with a non-existent ID. The API should return a not found error and not affect any other data.

Test retrieving a filtered and paginated list of post edit logs as a member. Apply different filters such as edit_member_id and time ranges, and verify pagination works correctly and returned entries match the filter criteria.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple posts and edits to generate post edit logs.
Edit posts to create log entries.

scenarios.draft: Test providing filter criteria that match no post edit logs (such as a random UUID as edit_member_id). The response should return an empty result set but remain a successful request.

Test that a moderator can retrieve, filter, and paginate post edit logs using valid search and sort criteria. Ensure the response contains the correct records and enforces permissions for the moderator role.

dependencies.purpose: Create posts and edits to populate post edit logs.
Edit posts to generate logs before searching as a moderator.

scenarios.draft: Test a search as moderator with criteria that will match no records (randomized values). Verify that a valid, but empty, paginated result is returned.

Test that a member can retrieve post history snapshots with a variety of complex filters and pagination options. Verify support for searching by post, by editing member, by edit type, and by created_at time ranges. Create multiple posts and perform multiple edits to generate varied histories first, using different edit types and reasons. Confirm the endpoint supports filtering by post, editor, type, and date accurately, and paginates correctly.

dependencies.purpose: Register members that will be used as post authors and editors.
Create a thread for context.
Create posts in the thread to have post histories attached.
Edit posts to generate post history snapshots for later retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to query the post histories list endpoint without valid authentication or via an unauthorized role, and confirm the request is rejected with an authorization error. This tests secure access.

Test that a moderator can access post history snapshots for moderation purposes. Create content as a member, perform post edits, then as a moderator, query history for specific posts and review edit tracking. Ensure comprehensive edit data is returned in compliance with schema for moderator role. Check filtering by edit_member_id, edit_type, and created_at.

dependencies.purpose: Register both member and moderator accounts.
Create a thread for posts to be edited.
Create posts by members to be edited.
Edit posts to ensure history entries are generated.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin user can list post edit histories using advanced search and filters for compliance/audit review. Populate threads with posts and edits by different members, then as an admin, use all primary filters (post, member, type, date). Ensure returned data matches schema and fulfills admin-level access needs. Test pagination with a large dataset.

dependencies.purpose: Register multiple members for varied history authorship.
Create one or more threads to generate post structures.
Create several posts to seed history.
Perform multiple edits to produce diverse history records.

scenarios.draft: Test a member retrieving the full details of their own post edit snapshot using the unique history id. After performing a post edit, fetch its history and verify all returned fields are as expected (id, post reference, edit type, old/new body, etc.).

dependencies.purpose: Register the member.
Create a thread for posts.
Create a post.
Edit the post to generate history.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to fetch a post history snapshot by providing an ID that does not exist. Confirm the API returns a proper error response (not found), ensuring error handling for invalid resource access.

Test that a moderator can access the full audit snapshot of any post by its history id. Create posts and make edits as different members, then retrieve the associated edit history as a moderator, confirming field-level access and audit details are present.

dependencies.purpose: Register member and moderator users.
Create a thread for context.
Members create and edit posts to produce histories.
Edit posts and generate history records.

scenarios.draft: Test paginated and filtered retrieval of polls as a moderator. This should cover scenarios such as: basic pagination (e.g., retrieving the first/second page), complex filtering (by thread, creator, anonymity, expiration status), and combining sort options (e.g., by most recent or soonest to expire). Ensure that anonymous and non-anonymous polls, expired and active polls, polls created by the requesting moderator and others, and multiple thread associations are properly returned respecting filters. Dependency on the poll creation endpoint is required to ensure test data coverage for all relevant cases.

dependencies.purpose: Create a variety of polls with differing thread associations, anonymity, expiration, creators, and configuration options for pagination and filter testing as a moderator.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a list of polls as an admin including filtering, sorting, and pagination. Coverage should include retrieving all polls, filtering by non-active/expired status, sorting by prompt or expiration, and verifying that admin can see polls across all members and threads regardless of ownership. Validation includes performance for large result sets, correct application of filter and sort criteria as described in business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a large, diverse poll set created by multiple members to ensure admin-level list, filter, and sort tests accurately reflect data spanning multiple users and thread contexts.

scenarios.draft: Test viewing detailed poll data as a member. Validate that a member can see details for an existing poll, including prompt, configuration, expiration, and thread association. Also test error cases such as requesting a poll that does not exist (expecting 404) and attempting to access a poll the member is not authorized to see (if such business rules apply). Set up dependencies to create several polls and use both valid and invalid poll IDs in retrieval tests.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one valid poll to be retrieved by its ID as a member.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can retrieve the details of any poll, regardless of ownership, examining fields such as prompt, anonymity, expiration, voting configuration, and creator. Test includes valid retrieval as well as error/edge cases such as non-existent poll ID (should return a 404 error). Ensure that role-based access control allows moderators broader poll visibility than regular members. Dependency: multiple polls with different creators and settings must be established for complete coverage.

dependencies.purpose: Create several polls with diverse configuration, creators, and thread associations to validate moderator's poll retrieval capability and error handling for invalid IDs.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can fetch detailed information for any poll using the poll's ID. Validation includes coverage for all data fields (prompt, anonymity, multiple choices, expiration, etc.), retrieval of polls created by different members, including expired and active polls, and correct error response for non-existent polls (404 error). Also verify that admin can view polls in all threads regardless of ownership and thread state.

dependencies.purpose: Create a variety of polls to cover scenarios of valid pull details access (diverse prompt, anonymity, expiration, ownership) and test non-existent ID retrieval for negative path validation.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving the details of a ban record by its ID when the record exists. First, create a ban record for a member or guest using the appropriate endpoint. Then, attempt to retrieve the ban using the GET endpoint and verify that all returned fields match the created record's values. This scenario confirms correct data retrieval and field mapping.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new ban record so its ID can be used to test the GET endpoint for existing records.

scenarios.draft: Test the system's response when attempting to retrieve a ban record by a non-existent or already-deleted ID. Expect the API to return the appropriate error (e.g., 404 not found), confirming correct handling of missing records and no data leakage occurs for invalid IDs.

Test successful creation of a new permanent ban for a member with all required fields provided and valid values (target member ID, admin ID, valid reason, timestamp, and optional notes). Verify the response contains the correct data and the ban is enforceable via later retrieval endpoints.

Test creating a permanent ban record for a guest, ensuring that only the required guest fields are supplied (guest_id instead of member_id). Confirm the ban appears in subsequent ban list/retrieval operations.

Attempt to create a ban with missing essential fields (e.g., no banned_member_id or banned_guest_id, or no reason). Expect validation to fail and the API to return an error specifying which fields are absent.
Attempt to create a ban for a non-existent member or guest ID. The API should return an error indicating the target does not exist, ensuring integrity of foreign key relationships across entities.

Attempt to create a new ban for a member who already has an active ban. The API should respond with a conflict or business rule error, confirming that duplicate bans for the same target are not allowed (if enforced by the business policy).

dependencies.purpose: First, create an initial ban for the member to establish the precondition for a duplicate ban attempt.

scenarios.draft: Test successful update of the reason and notes fields of an existing ban record by an admin. Initially, create a ban record. Then, update its mutable fields and verify the response reflects the changes and no other fields were altered.

dependencies.purpose: Create a ban record to update.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a ban with a non-existent ban ID. The API should return an error indicating that the record was not found, ensuring safe error handling for invalid update attempts.

Attempt to update a valid ban record using credentials of a user without admin rights or who is not the owner. API should reject the operation for insufficient permissions, confirming access control enforcement.

Attempt to update a ban with a payload including invalid or non-schema fields, or setting fields to invalid data types. The API should reject the request with a validation error, ensuring schema compliance is enforced for updates.

dependencies.purpose: Create a ban record to provide a valid ID for testing invalid payloads during update.

scenarios.draft: Test successful hard deletion of a ban record by its ID. Create a ban, then delete it via this endpoint. After deletion, verify that the record cannot be retrieved via the GET endpoint, confirming irreversibility.

dependencies.purpose: Create a ban record subject to deletion.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a ban with an invalid or already-deleted ID. API should return a not found error or similar, confirming correct handling of invalid deletion targets.

Test deletion attempt from a user with insufficient privileges (not an admin or not the creating admin). Verify that access is denied and the record remains unchanged, confirming permission checks are effective.

dependencies.purpose: Create a ban record to set up a valid, restricted deletion scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of post reactions, specifying valid filter criteria such as post ID, member ID, or reaction type. The API should return only matching records, confirming accurate filtering and pagination logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create post reaction records to ensure data exists for filter testing.

scenarios.draft: Test querying post reactions with filter parameters that match no records. The API should return an empty paginated result, not an error, confirming correct handling of zero-result searches.
Attempt to retrieve post reactions using invalid filter fields, unsupported data types, or out-of-schema keys. The system should respond with a validation error and not attempt to process the query.

Verify that a member can only retrieve reactions they are authorized to see, depending on their role and ownership. Create reactions as different members and attempt filtering as a non-owner. Confirm the API does not leak data outside the current member’s permissions.

dependencies.purpose: Create post reactions with different members to test data isolation and permission boundaries.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated, filtered, and sorted list of moderation actions as an admin. The test should cover filtering moderation actions by moderator_id, report_id, action_type, time ranges, and affected content IDs to ensure the system returns only matching records. Pagination logic should be validated (request multiple pages to ensure result consistency). Include scenarios for empty search results (filters with no match), invalid filter values (e.g. non-existent moderator_id), and overly broad queries (returning large datasets). Permission enforcement must be tested to confirm that only admins (not other roles) can access this endpoint.

Verify fetching a specific moderation action by its valid id as a moderator, confirming that all schema fields—id, moderator_id, report_id, affected_post_id, affected_member_id, action_type, action_description, action_timestamp—are returned and correctly populated. This requires first creating a moderation action record and then retrieving it via its id.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action and obtain the id for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test the scenario where a moderator attempts to fetch a moderation action that does not exist (invalid/nonexistent id). The system should respond with a not found error and must not leak information about other records or internal state.

Verify that an admin can retrieve the full details of a moderation action by a valid id, ensuring all schema fields are returned and correctly reflect the stored record. Requires creating a moderation action entry and then requesting it as an admin.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action as admin and obtain the id for detail retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to retrieve a moderation action with an invalid/nonexistent id as an admin and verify that the API returns a not found error, with no record data leak or system failure.

Test successful creation of a moderation action as a moderator by supplying all required schema fields (moderator_id, report_id, affected_post_id, affected_member_id, action_type, action_description, action_timestamp). Validate that the created record can be retrieved and matches the submitted values. This scenario verifies basic creation and storage of moderation actions.

Attempt to create a moderation action as a moderator while omitting one or more required fields (such as action_type or moderator_id). The system should reject the request and return a validation error indicating which field(s) are missing.

Test submission of a moderation action with invalid foreign keys for moderator_id, affected_post_id, affected_member_id, or report_id. The system must return an error for any non-existent references, ensuring referential integrity. This requires knowledge of existing records or the ability to attempt creation with randomly generated (but non-existent) UUIDs.

Verify that an admin can successfully create a moderation action by providing all required schema fields, and that the returned record contains accurate and complete information. The scenario should confirm admin authorization is effective and creation succeeds with proper input.

Attempt to create a moderation action as admin while omitting required fields (such as report_id or action_type). Confirm that the endpoint returns a validation error that clearly specifies the missing fields.

Test that admin attempts to create a moderation action using non-existent foreign key references (e.g., fake moderator_id or affected_post_id) are properly rejected by the system, enforcing referential integrity and error reporting.

Test fetching a specific search history record by its unique searchHistoryId. Begin by creating a search history record for a member using the POST /member//my/searchHistories endpoint, then retrieve it using GET /searchHistories/{searchHistoryId} to ensure all schema fields are returned correctly and the data matches what was inserted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new search history record and obtain its ID to use for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a search history record using a non-existent searchHistoryId. Attempt to GET /searchHistories/{searchHistoryId} with a randomly generated UUID that does not exist in the system, and verify that the response correctly returns an error indicating the record was not found.

Test listing search histories for the authenticated member where records exist. First, create multiple search history records using POST /member//my/searchHistories, then call PATCH /member//my/searchHistories with appropriate filter and pagination parameters. Validate that the returned list contains all and only the authenticated member's records, and that records marked as deleted (deleted_at set) are excluded.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple search history records for the authenticated member to ensure test data presence.

scenarios.draft: Test listing search histories for an authenticated member who has no search history records (or all are deleted). Authenticate as a member who has not created any search histories, call PATCH /member//my/searchHistories, and verify the paginated result is empty.

Test retrieving a specific search history record for the authenticated member by its searchHistoryId. First, create a new search history record using POST /member//my/searchHistories, then retrieve it using GET /member//my/searchHistories/{searchHistoryId}. Validate that the result includes all schema fields and only records owned by the authenticated member are accessible.

dependencies.purpose: Create a search history record and extract its ID to use for authenticated retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a search history record for an authenticated member using a searchHistoryId belonging to another user. First, create a search history record for a different member, then attempt to retrieve it using another authenticated session and expect a not found or unauthorized error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a search history record for a different member.

scenarios.draft: Test the successful creation of a search history record for the authenticated member. Send a valid payload to POST /member//my/searchHistories and verify that the response includes all the expected schema fields, and the returned data matches the input values appropriately, including correct association with the member ID.

Test failure scenario when attempting to create a search history record with missing required fields. Attempt to POST /member//my/searchHistories while omitting a required property (e.g., search_query) and verify the error response correctly identifies the missing field.

Test the successful update of a search history record owned by the authenticated member. Create a search history record using POST /member//my/searchHistories, then update allowed fields (such as search_query or used_filters) using PUT /member//my/searchHistories/{searchHistoryId}, and confirm that the updated data is reflected in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a search history record to update and retrieve its ID.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a search history record not owned by the authenticated member. Create a record for one member, then attempt to update it as another member using PUT /member//my/searchHistories/{searchHistoryId}, and validate that a not found or unauthorized error response is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a search history record for a different member to attempt unauthorized update.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a moderator can successfully update their own suspension record with valid schema-compliant fields. Use moderator authentication, ensure the targeted suspension record is owned by the authenticated moderator, and update allowed fields such as suspension_reason or suspension_ends_at. Confirm that the returned record reflects the updated values. Prerequisite: a valid suspension record must exist for the moderator.

dependencies.purpose: Create a suspension record that will be updated in this test; must be owned by the authenticated moderator.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a moderator cannot update a suspension record not owned by them. Attempt to update the suspension of another moderator and expect an authorization error. This scenario ensures strict ownership enforcement for the /my/ path.

dependencies.purpose: Create a suspension owned by a different moderator for negative test case.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin user can update their own suspension record through the /my/ endpoint, changing allowed fields such as suspension_reason or suspension_ends_at. Ensure the target record belongs to the admin performing the update. Check that changes are applied as expected and no non-schema fields are affected. Prerequisite: a suspension record exists for the admin as the moderator_id.

dependencies.purpose: Create a suspension for the admin to update in this scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempts to update non-existent or prohibited fields in a suspension record (such as undefined meta fields) are rejected with proper validation errors. This scenario ensures strong schema validation enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid suspension record for the admin prior to attempted invalid updates.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a moderator can successfully perform a hard delete of their own suspension record. Confirm that after deletion, the suspension cannot be retrieved. Ensure only owned suspensions can be deleted using the /my/ path. Prerequisite: create a suspension for the moderator to delete.

dependencies.purpose: Create a suspension for the moderator who will execute the hard delete operation.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a moderator cannot delete a suspension record owned by another moderator, and that the API returns the appropriate authorization or forbidden error. This ensures proper enforcement of ownership rules on deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create a suspension under a different moderator account for negative case testing.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin user can perform a hard delete on their own suspension record, ensuring the record is permanently removed. After deletion, verify the record is not retrievable. Prerequisite: an admin-owned suspension must exist.

dependencies.purpose: Create a suspension record for the admin, to later be deleted in this test.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin cannot delete a suspension not owned by them via the /my/ endpoint, confirming proper authorization enforcement. Attempt deletion of a different user’s suspension and expect an error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a suspension belonging to a different admin for negative case.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can successfully retrieve a paginated and filtered list of ban records, filtering on fields such as banned_member_id, banned_guest_id, and is_active. The test should set up multiple ban records, then query with different filtering and pagination options to ensure proper results are returned. Validate that records correspond to query filters and respect schema-only fields.

dependencies.purpose: Create ban records for both members and guests to populate the list and enable meaningful filtering scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Verify that filtering the bans list with criteria that match no records results in an empty result set. Set up with known state, then query using filters that do not correspond to any existing ban.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one ban record for a positive baseline, then query with non-matching filters for the negative case.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can successfully create a new incident report by providing valid values for all required schema fields: incident_code, status, reporter_id, description, created_at. The expected result is a new record in the incident reports table reflecting the provided data. Verify that the returned object contains all schema-defined fields and that business rules regarding enum values for status and required formats are enforced.

Test that attempting to create an incident report without mandatory fields (such as missing incident_code or description) results in a validation error. This ensures that any omitted required schema fields are properly rejected by the API and that a clear error message is returned to the admin user.

Test that when an admin tries to create an incident report using an invalid or unsupported enum value for the status field, the system rejects the request. Ensure that only schema-specified status values are valid and improper values return a validation error.

Test upper-bound length and business validation by submitting an incident report with an extremely long description field. This ensures that the API correctly enforces maximum allowed length and does not allow storage or response truncation or failure.

Test that a moderator can successfully create an incident report using the correct schema fields and that the record is properly associated with their moderator user ID. All required report values (incident_code, status, reporter_id, description, created_at) must be submitted. The result should be a valid incident report tied to the moderator, visible in subsequent queries.

Test case where a moderator attempts to submit two incident reports with the same incident_code (if code is supposed to be unique per system or type). The API should enforce the uniqueness constraint, if applicable, and return an error for the duplicate entry attempt. This verifies enforcement of unique business identifiers within the incident tracking process.

Test retrieving a specific incident report by its ID after it has been created. This validates that the system returns the correct record with all schema fields, accurately reflecting the data stored. Confirm that reading a known existing report returns the precise incident details as submitted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new incident report to ensure a valid incidentReportId exists for the retrieval test.
