scenarios.draft: Test attempting to fetch an incident report using a non-existent or malformed incidentReportId (e.g., random UUID, invalid format). The API should return a 404 not found error or a validation error as appropriate, confirming robustness against invalid lookup attempts.

Test that a moderator can successfully retrieve an incident report that was submitted by themselves using the correct incidentReportId. The returned data must match exactly what was submitted, and all schema fields must be present.

dependencies.purpose: Create an incident report as a moderator so the report is available for retrieval by the same role.

scenarios.draft: Test the behavior when a moderator attempts to retrieve an incident report with an ID that does not exist. The correct behavior is to return a 404 not found error without exposing unnecessary system or audit information.

Test updating an existing incident report by its ID, changing permitted fields such as status or description, and verifying that the update is correctly persisted in the database. The operation should return the updated incident report with the new values. Only existing schema fields may be changed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a fresh incident report to update, ensuring a valid incidentReportId exists.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an incident report and setting the status field to an invalid or unsupported value. The system should reject the update attempt and return a validation error consistent with the schema constraints, confirming strict type enforcement for enums.

dependencies.purpose: Create an incident report to enable an update test for negative enum value scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test the update operation using a non-existent incidentReportId. The system should return a not found error, confirming that only existing reports can be updated and that errors are clear and do not expose system internals.

Test attempting to update an incident report by omitting required fields (if required in PUT requests), to verify whether the system enforces the requirement to provide all necessary update data or can handle partial updates appropriately. The operation should return a validation error if required fields are missing.

dependencies.purpose: Create a sample report to attempt a partial update that omits some schema-mandatory fields.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an authenticated member can retrieve details of a specific post reaction using a valid post reaction ID. The test sets up a post and a post reaction by the member, then requests the reaction details by ID and checks that all expected schema fields are present and correct.

dependencies.purpose: Create a discussion thread for the test post.
Create a post in the created thread. A post is required to react to.
Create a post reaction by the authenticated member for the post.

scenarios.draft: Verify that requesting a post reaction by a nonexistent or invalid ID returns a not found or appropriate error. No actual post reaction is created for this test, and a random or deleted ID is used.

Test that a member can successfully create a post reaction. This involves setting up a thread, then a post, and finally submitting a valid reaction to that post. It verifies that a new reaction is recorded and returned according to schema.

dependencies.purpose: Create a discussion thread for the post and reaction.
Create a post in the created thread, which will be reacted to.

scenarios.draft: Verify that attempting to create a duplicate reaction (same user, same post, same reaction type) results in a uniqueness/constraint violation error. This test first creates a valid post reaction, then attempts to create an identical reaction by the same member for the same post.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a discussion thread for the test.
Create the post for reaction.
Create the first valid post reaction to be duplicated.

scenarios.draft: Test that creating a post reaction with an invalid or non-existent post ID is rejected with an appropriate error indicating the post does not exist.

Verify that the authenticated member can update their own post reaction, changing the reaction type. Precondition: a thread, a post, and a reaction record by the member already exist. The member changes the reaction (e.g., from 'like' to 'love'), and the result should reflect the new reaction type.

dependencies.purpose: Create a discussion thread.
Create a post for reaction.
Record an initial reaction by the member to update.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member cannot update a post reaction record they do not own. Set up a post reaction by one member, attempt an update as a different member, and assert that a forbidden or unauthorized error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread for a post.
Create the post to be reacted to.
Create the reaction as the original owner.
Add a second member for the non-owner update attempt.

scenarios.draft: Ensure a member is able to delete their own post reaction. Create a thread, a post, and a reaction by the member, then issue a delete for that reaction and confirm its removal.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a thread for the test.
Create a post in the thread.
Create a reaction that will be deleted by the member.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that a member cannot delete a post reaction they do not own. Create the reaction as one member, then attempt to delete as a different member and verify that a forbidden or appropriate error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread for the test.
Create a post in the thread.
Create a reaction with the first member.
Create a second member to perform the forbidden deletion attempt.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a member can retrieve a paginated, filterable list of post likes, specifying filters such as post ID or member ID. Set up multiple posts and likes, then assert that the list endpoint returns correct results according to filters and pagination settings.

dependencies.purpose: Create threads for test posts.
Create multiple posts to be liked.
Create like records on the posts for filter criteria.

scenarios.draft: Test the behavior when the list endpoint is called with filter criteria that match no post likes. Set up unrelated data, then request likes with a filter where there should be zero results and assert the empty result set.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread for an unrelated post.
Create an unrelated post for context.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully update a moderation action record owned by themselves using only the schema-allowed fields: action_description, action_type, affected_post_id, affected_member_id, and action_timestamp. Ensure that the updated details are correctly returned in the response, and the changes are accurately reflected in the record. The action id must reference a real moderation action owned by the moderator. Dependencies: the moderator must exist and must have previously created a moderation action with the given id.

dependencies.purpose: Assign moderator role to a member so that the test user has moderator privileges.
Create a moderation action owned by the moderator to set up for update testing.

scenarios.draft: Test that updating a moderation action with fields not present in the schema (such as a made-up field or attempt to change the id) is rejected with a validation error. This verifies strict schema adherence and helps prevent data corruption or security issues. Attempt the update with invalid fields and verify the response appropriately rejects the request without changing the stored action data.

dependencies.purpose: Assign moderator role so the test user is authorized.
Create a valid moderation action record for testing invalid field update.

scenarios.draft: Verify that attempting to update a moderation action not owned by the authenticated moderator (i.e., another moderator's record) is rejected due to permission checks. The scenario requires at least two moderator users: one creates a moderation action, the other attempts to update it and should receive a forbidden or not-authorized error response. This enforces business rules around action ownership and data privacy.

dependencies.purpose: Assign moderator roles to two members to simulate multiple moderators.
Create a moderation action with the first moderator for update attempts with the second.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can successfully update one of their own moderation action records by id, modifying only schema-allowed fields such as action_description, action_type, affected_post_id, affected_member_id, and action_timestamp. Verify that the update is persisted and response contains updated data. Admin must first create a moderation action for themselves to enable this test.

dependencies.purpose: Assign admin role so the test user has admin privileges.
Create a moderation action owned by the admin user to be updated in this scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to update a moderation action with undocumented or schema-forbidden fields (such as adding fields not defined or trying to change the id) results in validation errors, and the underlying record is not affected. This ensures the admin endpoint enforces schema correctness.

dependencies.purpose: Assign admin role so the test user has admin privileges.
Create a moderation action owned by the admin for update with invalid fields test.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that if an admin tries to update a moderation action record not owned by them (i.e., created by another admin or moderator), the attempt results in a forbidden or not-authorized error response. This scenario enforces update permission boundaries between admins. Requires two admin users for full test coverage.

dependencies.purpose: Assign admin roles to two distinct users to simulate two admin accounts.
First admin creates moderation action; second admin attempts the update.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully delete (hard-delete) their own moderation action record by id. The record is permanently removed from the system with no recovery possible, and confirm the action cannot be found after deletion. The moderator must have an existing moderation action before performing the delete.

dependencies.purpose: Assign moderator role to a member for proper permissions.
Create a moderation action record for the moderator to enable testing deletion.

scenarios.draft: Verify that attempting to delete a moderation action not owned by the current moderator (i.e., one created by another moderator) results in a forbidden or not-authorized error. This test upholds data ownership integrity. Involves two moderator users: one creates the record, the other attempts deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create two moderator users with the appropriate role assignment.
Have one moderator create an action so the other can attempt deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can hard-delete one of their own moderation action records by id. Once the operation is completed, the record must not be retrievable. The admin should first have created a moderation action record for this test.

dependencies.purpose: Assign admin privileges to the test user.
Create a moderation action record owned by the admin to test deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test that trying to delete a moderation action created by another admin or moderator using the current admin's credentials fails due to permission enforcement. This requires preparing two distinct admin users and demonstrating that one cannot delete the other's actions.

dependencies.purpose: Assign admin roles to two users for permission boundary checks.
One admin creates a moderation action; the other attempts unauthorized deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test the retrieval of a paginated and filtered list of warning logs issued by moderators to members. Provide different search and filter options (e.g., by moderator_id, warned_member_id, reason substring, issued_at range, or sorted by issued_at) in the request body, and verify that only matching warning logs are returned with correct pagination information. This scenario checks business logic for moderation log visibility and list accuracy. Assumes there are multiple warning logs in the system for a comprehensive query test.

dependencies.purpose: Assign moderator role so the test user can create warning logs.
Create several warning logs with different fields to populate data for list/filter testing.

scenarios.draft: Test that providing a filter which does not match any existing warning log (for example, a non-existent warned_member_id or a reason string not present in any entry) results in an empty list being returned. This scenario ensures correct handling of no-result cases without errors. This is important for UX and API predictability.

dependencies.purpose: Assign moderator role so the test user can create warning logs.
Create at least one warning log to ensure the table is not empty, then filter with a value that cannot match.

scenarios.draft: Test that an unauthorized or non-moderator user cannot retrieve the list of warning logs, resulting in an authorization error. Attempt to access the endpoint with a user lacking moderator or admin rights, and verify the response enforces proper authorization policies. This validates security and compliance measures around moderation log access.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular member without moderator/admin rights for negative access test.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an administrator can successfully hard-delete an existing platform policy record by its unique ID. First, create a new platform policy using POST /policyAudit/platformPolicies to ensure there is a policy to delete. Then, delete that policy with DELETE /policyAudit/platformPolicies/{platformPolicyId} and confirm the operation succeeds (e.g., 204 No Content or deletion confirmation) and that GET /policyAudit/platformPolicies/{platformPolicyId} for the same ID after deletion returns a not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a platform policy to ensure a valid record exists for deletion.
Verify that record creation and subsequent deletion are reflected in retrievable detail before and not found after.

scenarios.draft: Verify that attempting to delete a non-existent platform policy ID as an administrator results in a 404 not found or similar error. Attempt the DELETE operation with a randomly generated UUID that does not match any existing platform policy record and assert that the API responds with the appropriate error response, confirming safe handling of unknown IDs.

Test the retrieval of a paginated and filtered list of audit logs as an admin. The scenario should include:
- Using no filters to get a default paginated list.
- Applying filters for action_type, actor_id, or created_at range to ensure filtering works as intended.
- Verifying results are paginated and can be sorted as specified in the request body, and that results contain only schema-specified fields (id, action_type, description, actor_id, target_id, created_at).
- Ensuring that only authorized admin users can access this endpoint, while unauthorized users are denied access.

Verify that querying the audit log list with filter criteria that yield no results (such as an impossible actor_id or future time range) returns a valid paginated response with an empty list but no errors. This ensures the API gracefully handles empty result sets.

Verify the retrieval of a single audit log entry by its valid unique ID as an admin. First, perform or simulate an action that generates an audit log entry (such as creating a new policy, which should be logged if audit triggers are active). Then, retrieve the audit log by its ID and assert that the returned data matches the schema and that all required fields are present and accurate.

dependencies.purpose: Generate an auditable action by creating a platform policy, assuming this action is logged.
List audit logs to extract the ID of a recently created log entry for detail retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test the behavior when an admin attempts to fetch details of a non-existent audit log record using a random UUID. The endpoint should respond with a 404 or appropriate error, confirming secure no-leakage behavior for invalid IDs.

Verify admin retrieval of a list of incident reports with various filter and pagination options. The test should include:
- Requesting all incident reports with no filters for a default page.
- Using filters for specific status, incident_code, reporter_id, description keywords, or created_at ranges, verifying only matching records are returned.
- Testing pagination parameters to ensure results can be paged through correctly and fields match the schema only.

Submit a search with filters that cannot possibly match any incident reports (such as a random incident_code or a time range in the far future) to verify that the response is a valid page with an empty results array and does not return errors, confirming correct empty state behavior.
Attempt to access this endpoint with a non-admin, non-moderator account and assert that access is denied (401/403), confirming correct role-enforcement for sensitive incident data.

Verify that a user with moderator privileges can retrieve incident reports with filters or pagination, mirroring admin access but using a moderator session. Ensure all filtering, sorting, and pagination is reflected as described in the admin test, including schema-only field validation.

Use edge case filters with the PATCH body (such as start date in the far past, unusual status values, or large page sizes) and verify API stability and schema-compliance of results. Ensure the API does not crash, that empty or large result sets are handled correctly, and that invalid filter values trigger validation errors where applicable.

Attempt to list incident reports using a malformed or revoked session as a moderator and confirm the endpoint returns the appropriate unauthorized or session-expired error, preserving security for incident report data.

Test a successful update of an incident report by a moderator. First, create a new incident report using correct schema fields as a moderator. Then, attempt to update allowed fields (incident_code, status, reporter_id, description, updated_at) on this record. Ensure the response reflects the new values and only permits changes to fields within the schema. Ownership and permission enforcement should be validated so that only authorized moderators can update.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new incident report as a prerequisite so that an existing report is available to update.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update an incident report using an incidentReportId that does not exist. The system should return a not found error. Validate correct error handling for non-existent records and ensure no fields are mutated.

Test updating an incident report by including fields not present in the schema. The request should be rejected, and the API must return a validation error specifying the misuse of invalid properties. Confirm no update occurs and only schema-compliant fields are allowed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid incident report before attempting an invalid update.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update an incident report as an unauthorized user (e.g., as a member or guest instead of a moderator/admin). The API should return an unauthorized or forbidden error, preventing the operation.

dependencies.purpose: Create an incident report as a moderator so it exists to test improper permission for update.

scenarios.draft: Test successful hard deletion of an incident report by an admin. First, create a new incident report (using moderator or admin privilege), then delete it using the admin route. Confirm the record is irreversibly removed and cannot be retrieved afterward. Validate correct permissions and permanent deletion behavior.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new incident report so that an existing record is available for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete an incident report with a non-existent incidentReportId. Confirm that a not found error is returned and that no records are removed.
Attempt to perform deletion as a user who is not an admin (such as a member or moderator lacking proper access). The system should return a forbidden error and not execute any deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create an incident report with admin privilege to test deletion with insufficient permission.

scenarios.draft: Test successful hard deletion of an incident report by a moderator. First, a moderator creates a new incident report. Then, the report is deleted using the moderator endpoint. After deletion, attempts to retrieve the incident report should fail, confirming it was irreversibly removed.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a valid incident report entry to be deleted during the test.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete an incident report as an unauthorized actor (such as a member or guest). The request should be rejected with a forbidden error. Validate that only moderators and admins can perform this operation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid incident report to ensure there is a record for unauthorized users to attempt to delete.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete an incident report using a randomly generated UUID that does not correspond to any existing record. Confirm that the API returns a not found error and does not remove any data.

Test listing and searching appeals as an admin using a variety of search, filter, and pagination criteria. The test should cover filtering by status, outcome, appellant_id, and created_at date ranges, as defined in the schema. Also, check that sorting and pagination work properly. Validate that only appeals matching the query are returned and others are excluded.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple appeals with diverse data to ensure there are enough entries to test filtering and pagination as an admin.

scenarios.draft: Test searching for appeals as an admin using filter criteria that match no records. Confirm that the system returns an empty result set and no errors are raised.

Attempt to use the PATCH /admin/policyAudit/appeals endpoint as an unauthorized role (e.g., member or guest). Confirm the API returns a forbidden error, ensuring only admins and moderators can access this route.

Test listing and searching appeals records as a moderator, using filters such as status, appellant_id, incident_id, and created_at range. Confirm that only records matching the query are returned and pagination/sorting features act as expected. Coverage should affirm retrieval of only permitted data for the moderator role.

dependencies.purpose: Set up multiple appeal records with varied data so there are sufficient examples for searching and filtering as a moderator.

scenarios.draft: Test searching for appeals as a moderator using criteria that do not match any entries. Validate that an empty result set is provided, and pagination metadata are correct.
Attempt to use the PATCH /moderator/policyAudit/appeals endpoint as a role lacking moderator privileges (e.g., member, guest). The API should return a forbidden error and prevent access.

Verify that an authenticated member can successfully retrieve the details of a mention they own by its unique ID. First, create a member, then create a post, and create a mention referencing this member in the post. Use the resulting mention's ID to fetch the mention. Check that all predefined schema fields are present in the response and match what was created.

dependencies.purpose: Create a mention to obtain a valid mention ID for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test behavior when trying to retrieve a mention by an ID that does not exist. Attempt to fetch a mention with a random/non-existent UUID as the ID and verify that the system returns a suitable not found error response.

Verify that a member cannot retrieve details of a mention they do not own (i.e., their member ID does not match mentioned_member_id). Setup: register two members, create a post, and then create a mention for member1 where only member2 is authenticated during GET. Expect a forbidden or not found error, depending on business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create a mention assigned to a different member to test access control.

scenarios.draft: Validate that an authenticated member can create a new mention by supplying a valid post and mentioned member. Setup: Create two members and a post, then create a mention linking the post to the second member. Check for successful creation and response fields compliance with schema.
Check that creating a mention with a non-existent post ID fails with an appropriate error due to foreign key violation. Try to use a random or invalid post UUID and verify error.

Ensure creation fails if the mentioned_member_id does not correspond to an existing member. Attempt to create a mention using a non-existent member UUID and expect a clear error indicating foreign key constraint failure.

Attempt to create a mention while not authenticated (guest or logged out user). Verify that the system blocks the request with an appropriate authorization error since only authenticated members may create mentions.

Confirm that an authenticated member can update their own mention entry, changing either the parent post or the mentioned_member_id to another valid entity. Setup: Register two members, create two posts, and a mention. Attempt to change the mention to refer to the second member or another post, and verify successful update and schema correctness.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial mention to perform the update operation.

scenarios.draft: Test the failure case where a member tries to update an owned mention to reference a non-existent post. Expect an error indicating foreign key violation.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial mention to perform the update operation.

scenarios.draft: Try to update a mention owned by another member. Setup: create member1 and member2; member1 creates a mention; member2 attempts to update it using the same ID. The system should reject the request with a forbidden error, enforcing record ownership.

dependencies.purpose: Create the mention owned by member1 to test forbidden access for member2.

scenarios.draft: Confirm that a member can successfully hard-delete a mention record they own, removing it from the system. Setup: Create a member and a mention, then perform the DELETE with authentication. Verify that the mention is no longer retrievable afterward and cannot be recovered.

dependencies.purpose: Create a mention to obtain an ID for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Validate that attempting to delete a mention not owned by the member fails with a forbidden or not found error, thus enforcing row-level data access control.

dependencies.purpose: Create the mention as a different member to test forbidden delete.

scenarios.draft: Test that an authenticated member receives a paginated and filterable list of their own notifications. Setup: Register a member and create several notifications for them, then list with/without various filter or pagination settings. Verify response correctness, ownership enforcement, and pagination compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create notifications for the test member in batch, to prepare data for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Check that advanced filtering and searching parameters (e.g., filtering by notification type, opened status, or title) are honored in the list results. Setup: Create multiple notifications with different values for searchable fields, then test search and filter capabilities, verifying only matching notifications are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create notifications with various filterable attributes for testing advanced list options.

scenarios.draft: Validate that notifications soft-deleted (deleted_at set) are not returned in the list of active notifications. Setup: Create notifications, soft-delete some using the DELETE operation, then fetch and check that only non-deleted notifications appear in the result.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple notifications and soft-delete some via DELETE to test filtering of deleted records.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of platform policies with different filters, sorting, and pagination options as an admin. Ensure that filtering by title, policy_code, is_active, and sorting by published_at/updated_at works correctly. Scenario covers: (1) default/all records, (2) filter by title substring, (3) filter by is_active=false, (4) sorting by updated_at descending, (5) pagination boundaries (first/last page), and (6) requesting with empty or invalid filter keys. Expect only actual schema fields in results, no extra or missing properties. If schema fields do not exist or filters are invalid, backend should ignore or raise a validation error. Only policies accessible by admin role should be returned. No dependency on specific data creation but relies on having at least several policies in the system to test effective filtering and paging behaviors.

dependencies.purpose: Create several platform policy records with varying titles, codes, active statuses, and published_at dates to ensure the list operation can be meaningfully tested against diverse data.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a new platform policy by an admin. Supply all required fields with valid data: policy_code (unique), title, policy_text, is_active. Confirm that the API returns the complete newly created record with all schema fields correctly set, and that published_at and updated_at are automatically handled by the server. Verify that the new policy can be retrieved via GET /policyAudit/platformPolicies/{platformPolicyId}.

Test failure scenario when attempting to create a platform policy with a policy_code that already exists. Attempt to create two policies with the same policy_code and different titles. System should reject the second attempt, enforcing unique constraint on policy_code and returning a conflict or validation error response. This checks proper business rule enforcement for uniqueness.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first platform policy with a unique policy_code to establish the precondition for a duplicate attempt.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a single platform policy by its ID as an admin. Start by creating a policy, then fetch it using its returned id. Validate that all returned fields exactly match the schema, and the id, code, and text match what was submitted. If the id does not exist, the system must return a not-found error. Check that only users with admin role may access this endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Create a platform policy to retrieve, so the platformPolicyId is valid.

scenarios.draft: Test the behavior when an admin tries to fetch a platform policy with an ID that does not exist in the system. Ensure a proper not-found (404) error is returned, and that the system does not leak any data about other records. This validates correct error handling for invalid lookups.

Test successful update of an existing platform policy by an admin. Update mutable fields such as policy_text, title, or is_active, using the id of an existing policy. Verify that the response contains updated values, no changes to immutable fields, and that a subsequent GET reflects the new data. Only schema fields should be in input and output. Updates to is_active and policy_text should persist as stored.

dependencies.purpose: Create a policy to update, establishing a valid platformPolicyId.

scenarios.draft: Test the behavior when updating a platform policy by an invalid/nonexistent platformPolicyId. Attempt the update as admin and verify a not-found (404) is returned, and that no other records are affected by the request.

Test authorization by simulating a non-admin user attempting to update a policy via this endpoint. Attempt a valid update payload as a user with insufficient privileges (e.g., member role), expect an access denied error. Policy should not change in system.

dependencies.purpose: Create a policy as admin for update attempt.

scenarios.draft: Test successful hard deletion of a business rule by an admin. Create a business rule, then delete it via its id. Confirm the record is permanently removed and cannot be retrieved via GET afterward. Test validates compliance with hard delete, not soft delete, as the schema supports only direct removal.

dependencies.purpose: Create a business rule to obtain a valid businessRuleId for deletion test.

scenarios.draft: Test hard delete request for a business rule with an invalid or randomly generated businessRuleId. Ensure system responds with a not-found (404) and does not remove or reveal any other records.

Attempt to delete an existing business rule using a user with insufficient authorization (e.g., member or moderator role). The request must be rejected with an access denied error, and the rule should remain untouched.

dependencies.purpose: Create a business rule as admin, then test unauthorized deletion attempt.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of a notification by its notificationId for an authenticated member. First, create a member and a notification assigned to this member. Then, retrieve the notification by its ID and verify all notification fields are returned, the ID matches, and ownership is correct.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to represent the authenticated user who will receive notifications.
Create a new notification belonging to the registered member that can be retrieved in this scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when attempting to retrieve a notification by an ID that does not exist or is not owned by the authenticated member. Attempt to fetch a notification using a random UUID that has not been assigned or one that belongs to another member, and verify that an appropriate error (not found or forbidden) is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Register two test members for permission testing or error simulation.
Create a notification for the first member; use an unrelated ID for the not-found and forbidden tests.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new notification for the authenticated member with valid required fields. After registering a member, use the endpoint to create a notification with proper type, title, and body fields. Verify the returned notification contains all expected schema fields, the owner matches the member, and values match the request.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member who will be the authenticated user/owner of the notification.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when required fields are missing or invalid in the notification creation request. Attempt to create a notification for the member with omitted type or title field and verify that a validation error response is received, confirming correct enforcement of schema requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member who will be the test owner for the notification creation attempt.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a notification belonging to the authenticated member. Register a member, create a notification for them, and then update fields such as title, body, or opened flag. Verify that the returned notification reflects the updated values and that non-updatable fields remain unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to act as the authenticated user.
Create a notification owned by the member that will be updated in this scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when attempting to update a notification that does not exist or is not owned by the member. Attempt to update a notification with a random UUID or one belonging to another member, and confirm an error response (not found or forbidden) is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Register two members for ownership and permission testing.
Create a notification for the first member. Use unrelated or unauthorized notificationId for error scenario.

Create a notification which will be deleted via soft deletion in this test.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling for attempts to delete a notification not belonging to the authenticated user or using a non-existent notificationId. Attempt to delete a notification with an unauthorized or random ID and validate that the system returns a forbidden or not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Register two members for ownership/authorization test.
Create a notification for the first member. Use second member or random ID for negative test.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of alerts for the authenticated member. Register a member and create multiple alert records with varying attributes (type, severity, is_active). Request the alert listing with different filters (e.g., type, severity, is_active) and pagination parameters, verifying that results match filter criteria and correct records are returned.

scenarios.draft: Test the listing endpoint for a member who has no alert records. Register a new member and request their alert listing, verifying an empty result set and no errors.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully update their own issued warning log record by ID. The scenario consists of creating a warning log as a moderator, then updating the warning reason or other schema-allowed fields (but not immutable fields). Confirm that the response reflects the updated values per the schema and that permissions are enforced (i.e., only the creator moderator may update their own log).

dependencies.purpose: Create a warning log as the moderator, obtain the log ID for subsequent update.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a moderator is forbidden from updating a warning log they did not create (ownership enforcement). Attempt to update a warning log created by another moderator and confirm that the system returns an appropriate authorization error, with no update performed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a warning log as a different moderator (to simulate an 'other user' log record).

scenarios.draft: Test updating a warning log with invalid or non-schema fields in the request body. Attempt to include properties not present in the warning logs table, and confirm that the system rejects the operation with validation errors, ensuring strong schema compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create a mod-owned warning log that will attempt to be updated with off-schema/inappropriate fields.

scenarios.draft: Ensure an admin user is able to update their own issued warning log by ID, modifying fields like warning_reason in accordance with the schema. The scenario should include log creation by admin, update, and verifying response contains all expected updated data.

dependencies.purpose: Create a warning log as admin for update test.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin attempting to update a warning log they do not own is prohibited from making changes, and the system responds with a suitable error (e.g., forbidden or not found).

dependencies.purpose: Create a warning log under a different moderator to validate admin cannot update others' logs via /my/ path.

scenarios.draft: Test the system's response when an admin attempts to update a warning log with invalid fields or non-schema properties. The update should be rejected with a validation error, and no data should be changed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a warning log as admin for schema compliance validation.

scenarios.draft: Test the scenario where a moderator deletes their own warning log by ID. After creation of a new log, perform hard delete using the relevant endpoint and confirm the record is no longer retrievable and is fully removed from the database.

dependencies.purpose: Create a warning log for deletion by the same moderator.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a warning log owned by another moderator. The scenario validates that only the owner can delete their own warning log; other users must receive a forbidden or not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a warning log with a separate moderator user for negative permission testing.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a warning log by a random or previously deleted ID. Confirm the API returns a not found (404) or similar error and does not crash or present ambiguous behavior. This ensures robust error handling for deletion of nonexistent resources.
Verify that an admin can delete their own warning log record by ID. The scenario involves creation then deletion, followed by checking that the deleted record cannot be fetched anymore.

dependencies.purpose: Create a warning log as an admin to set up the delete operation.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin user cannot delete another moderator's warning log using the /my/ path. The system should return a forbidden or not found error when a non-owned record is targeted for deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create a warning log via a different moderator to simulate ownership conflict for admin.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a warning log with an ID that does not exist or has already been deleted. Expect a 404 or relevant error without affecting stability of the endpoint. This validates system robustness and proper error feedback for end users.

Test that a moderator can retrieve a paginated and filtered list of suspension records, using combinations of filters such as by suspended_member_id, moderator_id, or suspension window. Validate that the results are accurate and pagination works as intended. Also verify role-based access control to ensure only authorized users can see this data.

dependencies.purpose: Create several suspension records for robust query testing.

scenarios.draft: Test the case where the filters used will result in no matching suspension records (e.g., using a random or non-existent suspended_member_id). Ensure the API responds gracefully with an empty results list and no error.

Attempt to query the suspension list using off-schema filter fields or invalid sorting keys. Confirm the API returns a schema validation error, refusing unsupported or non-schema filter/sort parameters.

Attempt to retrieve the suspension list as a user without proper authorization (not a moderator or admin). Confirm the API returns a forbidden or access denied error, enforcing role-based access control.

Test successful creation of an appeal by an admin, providing all required fields (appeal_code, status, appellant_id, incident_id, outcome, created_at, updated_at). This scenario confirms that when an admin supplies data strictly matching schema fields, the appeal record is created and returned with all properties correctly set. Prior to this, an incident report must be created to provide a valid incident_id reference. Appellant_id can reference an existing member or be null for certain business flows. This verifies end-to-end appeal registration for compliance workflows.

dependencies.purpose: Create an incident report to supply a valid incident_id for the appeal. This must be performed first to maintain referential integrity.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to create an appeal with a missing required field, such as omitting appeal_code or status. The scenario verifies that the system enforces required field validation, returning an error and not creating the appeal. Confirm that appropriate validation messages are returned to the admin client upon failure.

dependencies.purpose: Create an incident report so an incident_id is available, mirroring real creation flows.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of an appeal referencing an incident_id that does not exist in the incident reports table. This scenario ensures integrity checks are enforced, expecting a foreign key error or not found response. The admin user attempts to create an appeal linked to a fake or deleted incident_id, and the system must reject the request, preserving data consistency.

Test the creation of a new appeal by a moderator, filling all schema fields properly. Validate that moderator privileges allow creation with valid incident_id and proper status/appeal_code fields. This scenario confirms the workflow for moderators to submit appeals related to incidents under their management responsibilities. Ensure the incident_id used is real and points to an existing incident report.

dependencies.purpose: Create an incident report that the moderator can reference when creating the appeal.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to create an appeal as a moderator using an invalid status value (not part of allowed status enums). This scenario tests strict server-side status enum validation, ensuring that submissions failing enum checks are rejected and descriptive error messages returned.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a valid incident reference; test focuses on appeal status field validation.

scenarios.draft: Fetch an appeal by its valid id as a member, confirming that the endpoint returns the complete appeal information if the member is authorized to see it. This ensures permission checks are respected and the proper schema fields are returned. The appeal must be created first to ensure its existence.

dependencies.purpose: Create an incident for the new appeal.
Create the appeal as an admin so its id can be retrieved and supplied for this test.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to fetch an appeal by an id that does not exist as a member. Confirm the system returns a not found error or the correct error response code without exposing unnecessary information. This validates not found logic and proper error handling for missing records.

Attempt to fetch an appeal by id that belongs to another user, where the authenticated member is not the appellant nor authorized. This scenario tests authorization logic and that forbidden access is properly denied with a relevant error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create an incident for the appeal.
Create the appeal as a different member/admin for cross-user permission test.

scenarios.draft: Admin retrieves an existing appeal by its id, confirming that all fields defined in the schema are returned, and that access control for admin is enforced. The test also checks the pathway for review or audit scenarios. The appeal must exist prior to execution.

dependencies.purpose: Create an incident for linking to the appeal.
Create the appeal, capturing its id for the fetch operation.

scenarios.draft: Try to fetch a non-existent appeal by a random id as an admin. The scenario validates proper error reporting and that no sensitive data or internal error states are leaked. Expect a not-found error code or message following best API practices.

Moderator queries an appeal by its id, checking that all appeal details are returned if authorized. Test verifies moderator audit and review workflows are supported and schema compliance for returned data. Ensure the appeal is created before execution.

dependencies.purpose: Provide incident linkage for the appeal.
Create the appeal as a moderator and get the id to use in this scenario.

scenarios.draft: Moderator attempts to fetch an appeal by an id that doesn't exist. This checks for correct not found handling, ensures no error leakage, and validates security posture for moderator access.

Test successful deletion (hard delete) of a post edit log owned by the authenticated member. The member first creates a post, edits it (creating an edit log), and then deletes the corresponding post edit log via this endpoint. Ensure that the log is no longer accessible after deletion and that only the log owner can delete it.

dependencies.purpose: Register or ensure existence of authenticated member to serve as log owner.
Create a new thread for associating posts to test edit log actions.
Create a new post in the created thread (by the member).
Edit the created post, which should trigger a post edit log entry.

scenarios.draft: Test that deletion fails with a forbidden error if an authenticated member attempts to delete a post edit log not owned by them. Set up two members, have one member create an edit log, and then attempt deletion with the other member's identity. Expect a proper error response (forbidden/unauthorized).

dependencies.purpose: Register or ensure existence of both members (two different accounts).
Create a new thread for posts and edit logs.
Create a new post as member A.
Edit the post as member A to create a post edit log.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to delete a post edit log that does not exist returns the appropriate error (not found), confirming proper handling of invalid IDs or already-deleted logs.

Test retrieving a filtered and paginated list of thread archive records as a member. First, create one or more archived threads and confirm that the API returns the expected records when filtering and paginating. Check result size, content, and pagination meta-data.

Create multiple threads as members for subsequent archiving.
Archive (soft-delete) these threads to generate thread archive records.

scenarios.draft: Test filtering the thread archive list as admin by the archive_reason field. Archive threads for different reasons, then retrieve archives that only match a target reason.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure at least one admin user exists.
Create threads to be archived for multiple test reasons.
Archive (soft-delete) the threads using different archive reasons.

scenarios.draft: Test the successful retrieval of a thread archive record by id for an authenticated member. Create and archive a thread, then fetch the archive details to confirm data integrity and ownership or access permissions.

dependencies.purpose: Register or authenticate a member who will own the archive record.
Create and own a thread for archiving.
Archive the thread to create a thread archive record.

scenarios.draft: Test that requesting details for a non-existent thread archive id returns a not found error, confirming proper error handling for invalid archive ids.

Test that an authenticated member cannot access a thread archive record they do not own if such access restrictions apply. Create and archive a thread under one member, then attempt to access as a different member. Confirm proper error or access denial according to business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Register at least two members with distinct identities.
First member creates and archives (soft-deletes) a thread.

Proceed to update updatable fields such as status and outcome using this PUT endpoint. Verify that the updates are applied correctly and that fields not in the schema cannot be updated (e.g., ensure non-schema fields are ignored or trigger validation errors). The test confirms that a member may update only eligible schema fields and not invent new ones, and that an updated_at timestamp is changed as appropriate.

Use a newly created appeal as the update target. Prepare a request containing extra properties or invalid field values and submit via PUT. Confirm the API rejects the request, gives appropriate error feedback, and makes no changes to underlying data.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new appeal as owned by the test member to ensure permission for update.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member cannot update an appeal which is not owned by them. Create one appeal as another member and then authenticate as the test member. Attempt to update the other member's appeal via this endpoint. Confirm that the operation is rejected with a forbidden or permission-denied response and that the underlying data remains unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create an appeal as a separate (non-test) member to be used as the non-owned target.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can update any appeal in the system regardless of creator. Create an appeal as a regular member and use the admin role to change status and outcome via this endpoint. Verify the fields are updated correctly and limitations on schema-enforced values are respected. This test proves admin privilege and correct update logic for all eligible fields, as per business rules.

scenarios.draft: Verify that the admin cannot update an appeal with invalid data, such as disallowed enum values or missing required fields. Use a real appeal as the update target, submit an update request with bad data, and check that the API rejects the operation with a validation error and leaves the record unaltered.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that attempting to update an appeal that does not exist (invalid appealId) results in a not found error. Use a randomly generated but unused appealId as the target for the PUT request and verify the system's response is a 404 or equivalent, with no side effects in the system state.

Test that a member can delete their own appeal via a hard-delete operation. Start by creating an appeal as the test member; then call the DELETE endpoint with its appealId. Confirm response indicates successful deletion, the record is removed from the system, and subsequent GETs for the id return not found.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member cannot delete an appeal not owned by them. First, create an appeal as a different user. scenarios.draft: Ensure that trying to delete an appeal by specifying a non-existent appealId returns a not found or similar error. Choose a random UUID not in use, send DELETE, and check that the response signals the absence of the record and no system side effects occur.

Test that an admin can hard-delete any appeal in the system, regardless of its original creator. First create an appeal as any member, then as admin, issue a DELETE call for that appealId. Check that the record is removed and cannot be fetched afterward.

dependencies.purpose: Create an appeal as a setup for admin deletion test.

scenarios.draft: Test admin behavior when trying to delete an appeal record that does not exist. Pick an unused/random appealId, send DELETE with admin authentication, verify a not found response, and that no data is affected.

Test that an authenticated member can successfully retrieve an alert belonging to their account by providing a valid alertId. The test should confirm that all schema fields (id, discussionboard_member_id, type, severity, title, body, is_active, created_at, resolved_at) are correctly returned. Ownership checks must ensure the alert belongs to the user and does not expose alerts of other members. Only accessible by the owner.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving an alert with an alertId that does not exist in the system. The system should return a not found error (404) or equivalent error message, and should not expose any sensitive data.

Test that an authenticated member cannot retrieve an alert that belongs to another user. Attempting to fetch an alertId not owned by the requesting member should result in a forbidden or not found error, confirming proper ownership enforcement.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new alert for the authenticated member with valid type, severity, title, body, and is_active fields. Confirm that only schema fields are set and no extra/non-existent fields are included.
Test that creating an alert with a missing required field (e.g., type or title) fails as expected, returning a proper validation error for the missing property.

Test that an authenticated member can update fields of their own alert, such as is_active and resolved_at, by providing the correct alertId. The update should only allow changes to schema-defined fields and return the updated alert record. Ownership and schema compliance should be enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create an alert for the user to update in this test.

scenarios.draft: Test that an authenticated member cannot update an alert record which is not their own. Changes attempted on an alertId belonging to another user should fail with a forbidden or not-found error. This validates enforcement of ownership/authorization rules.

scenarios.draft: Test that if the request body includes fields not present in the schema or attempts to update non-updatable fields (such as id or discussionboard_member_id), the API rejects the update with a proper schema validation error. Only allowed fields should be permitted for update.

Test that providing an unknown or non-schema field in the filter criteria results in a validation error or is cleanly ignored, with no effect on the results. Validate that only schema fields are operable in filtering.

Create the initial post like before attempting the duplicate action.
